title: Infer alert footprint and trigger snapshotting for swift on-call diagnostics
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds an adaptive alert-footprint estimator and a defensive snapshot trigger for on-call summaries; no user-visible API changes; improves mean time to triage for noisy alerts.

description: Context: on-call teams frequently receive noisy alerts that lack sufficient context to triage quickly. Current incident-bot summaries include raw alert payloads but lack a fast indicator of whether a full memory/heap/kv snapshot is likely to be useful. Motivation: reduce mean time to investigate (MTTI) and mean time to triage (MITT) by only triggering heavy snapshot collection when the alert footprint indicates a high diagnostic value and to capture a compact snapshot with request and environment metadata. What I changed: implemented a lightweight footprint estimator that scores alerts using rule-based heuristics and lightweight learned signals (error rate, service churn, presence of stack or key markers, recent similar-alert counts), added a snapshot trigger that evaluates the estimator score plus local rate-limit state before launching snapshot collection, and exposed a new on-call summary field snapshot_suggested for UIs and runbook automations to render a one-click capture action. Design notes: the estimator executes on the alert processing path as a fast stateless function with a median execution time under 1ms and consults a TTL cache for recent related-alert counts; the trigger enforces per-service quotas and a global leaky-bucket backoff window to avoid amplification; the snapshot runner executes collection in a sandboxed job, performs a deterministic redaction pass to remove secrets, writes a manifest of removed keys, compresses the artifact, and stores it with cryptographic integrity metadata. Tests and validation: added unit tests for estimator heuristics and nil/legacy metadata handling, integration tests that simulate alert bursts to validate rate limiting and artifact retention, and CI smoke tests to ensure no regression in processing latency. Metrics and observability: added incidentbot.alert_footprint_score, incidentbot.snapshot_triggered_total, and incidentbot.snapshot_rate_limited_total; included dashboard panel suggestions and recommended thresholds in the playbook. Operational considerations: default configuration is feature-gated off for hosted low-tier accounts, snapshot artifacts are redacted by default and TTLed after configurable retention, and quotas can be tuned per-customer for Dedicated/Private deployments. Backwards compatibility: alerts without rich metadata fall back to conservative heuristics and will rarely trigger snapshots unless correlated evidence exists. Checklist: - Add estimator and trigger code (done) - Add unit and integration tests (done) - Add documentation and playbook snippet (done) - Add metrics and dashboard suggestions (done) - Validate CI and load-local smoke tests (done) Review conversation highlights: Samir Gupta requested unit tests for the edge case of missing metadata; author added nil guards and tests. Priya Nair requested default redaction and manifest of removed keys; author added redaction pass and tests. Diego Ramos suggested moving the rate-limiter into shared quota package; refactor completed and usages updated. CI summary: initial CI run flagged a flaky timing assertion in integration-azure-1; adjusted test timeouts and reran, all checks green on final run (unit, integration, lint, build, e2e-smoke). Merge decision: squash-merge after approvals and green CI. Related tasks: resolves ENG-1427 and SUP-831. Operational docs: docs/oncall/alert-footprint.md contains tuning guidance and playbook snippets for on-call teams; default behavior is conservative and opt-in for hosted tier.
